dedupe_keys.name: farm business survey england and wales special licence access uk data service series from 1982

description: The Farm Business Survey is conducted each year to collect business information from about 2,400 farms in England and Wales, covering the financial position and the physical and economic performance of farm businesses, to inform policy and compare groups of farms by region, type, size or farmer characteristics. The UK Data Service record for the 2012-2013 special licence study says the second edition (February 2015) added farmer and household income, tenanted land, English fertiliser use and livestock weight and feed data, plus environmental and labour data for Wales, and that grid references in Section A were removed to protect participants. It is published by the UK Data Service (2nd edition, 2019) for the Rural Business School at Duchy College, as part of a series from 1982, under Special Licence access, so use needs registration and an approved application; the fee and file formats are not stated on the page read. Coverage is England and Wales. Caveats: locations are withheld and it is a sample of commercial farms. For simulation it gives farm-level costs, inputs and incomes to model how input price shocks, disease outbreaks or disrupted supply affect farm viability. Related catalogue records include the Defra June Survey of Agriculture and Horticulture and the EU Farm Sustainability Data Network.
